what: Per-record Lean status, relation note and Comparator status copied from the papers' evidence mapping, keyed by graph record id. The graph schema has no field for them.

short.res-weighted-support.label: res:weighted-support
short.res-weighted-support.title: a weighted condition on the support
short.res-weighted-support.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones, with $A\subseteq\Npos$ written as $0\notin A$ and $W_{b,P}(A)<\infty$ written as summability over $A$ for some finite nonempty set $P$ of primes. The fixed-base statement and, under (W), irrationality at every $b\ge2$ for every infinite subset are the two parts of `divisibilityWeightedClaim`; heredity under the fixed-base condition is `finitePrimeWeighted_fixedBase_hereditary`.

short.thm-variable-fractional-cover.label: thm:257-variable-fractional-cover
short.thm-variable-fractional-cover.title: A summable family of divisor majorants
short.thm-variable-fractional-cover.relation_note: The Lean statement has the same hypotheses and conclusion as the printed one, with $F_j\subseteq\Npos$ written as $0\notin F_j$ and the index $j\ge1$ shifted to start at $0$. Lean assumes each $C_j$ finite, which the printed summability hypothesis already implies.

short.res-mixed-supports.label: res:mixed-supports
short.res-mixed-supports.title: mixed weighted and cover supports
short.res-mixed-supports.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusion as the printed theorem, with $E\subseteq\Npos$ written as $0\notin E$. A cover satisfying (V), with its index $j\ge1$ shifted to start at $0$, is `mixedSupportClaim`; the positive-weight variant, with weights $\eta_j>0$, $\sum_j\eta_j=1$ and $\sum_jC_j\eta_j^{-\alpha_j}/(2^{\alpha_j}-1)<\infty$, is `arbitraryWeightMixedSupport_allBase_hereditary`.

short.res-mixed-supports.label: thm:257-mixed-supports
short.res-mixed-supports.title: mixed weighted and cover supports
short.res-mixed-supports.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusion as the printed theorem, with $E\subseteq\Npos$ written as $0\notin E$. A cover satisfying the summability condition of the cover theorem, with its index $j\ge1$ shifted to start at $0$, is `mixedSupportClaim`; the positive-weight variant, with weights $\eta_j>0$, $\sum_j\eta_j=1$ and $\sum_jC_j\eta_j^{-\alpha_j}/(2^{\alpha_j}-1)<\infty$, is `arbitraryWeightMixedSupport_allBase_hereditary`.

short.res-weighted-cover-incomparability.label: res:weighted-cover-incomparability
short.res-weighted-cover-incomparability.title: incomparable support criteria
short.res-weighted-cover-incomparability.relation_note:
The two Lean statements supply the two hosts separately, with a positive support written as $0
otin E$ and a cover satisfying (V) indexed from $0$. `exists_weighted_not_strengthened_host` gives an infinite $E$ with $E\in\mathcal W_2$ and $E
otin\mathcal C$; `exists_strengthened_not_old_or_weighted_host` gives an infinite $V$ with $V\in\mathcal C$, $V
otin\mathcal W_b$ for every integer $b\ge2$, and non-summable reciprocals, which for nonnegative terms is $\sum_{a\in V}1/a=\infty$. Each adds further conclusions. The Lean host $V$ is a squarefree divisor-cube host with its own row schedule; the bounded-mass fresh-prime construction printed in the proof is an ordinary proof.

short.res-strict-mixed-supports.label: res:strict-mixed-supports
short.res-strict-mixed-supports.title: a support requiring the mixed criterion
short.res-strict-mixed-supports.reason: the new host existence claim has not been formalised; the mixed implication it invokes is already checked

short.res-reciprocal-support.label: res:reciprocal-support
short.res-reciprocal-support.title: reciprocal-summable supports
short.res-reciprocal-support.relation_note: The Lean statement has the same hypotheses and conclusion as the printed one, except that $A$ may contain $0$; the term at $0$ is $0$ in both $\sum_{a\in A}1/a$ and $X_A(b)$ under the convention $1/0=0$.

short.res-period.label: res:period
short.res-period.title: the exact denominator period
short.res-period.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones, with $F\subseteq\Npos$ written as $0\notin F$; coprimality of $D_F$ and $b$ is proved without assuming $F$ nonempty. The order is the multiplicative order of $b$ modulo $D_F$, which is $1$ when $D_F=1$, as in the convention $\operatorname{ord}_1(b)=1$.

short.res-one-over-twenty-one-frontier.label: res:one-over-twenty-one-frontier
short.res-one-over-twenty-one-frontier.title: integer-quotient tests for $`1/21`$
short.res-one-over-twenty-one-frontier.relation_note: Item 2 follows from a Lean criterion with a weaker hypothesis: $1/21\in\Ach$ whenever $(s_R+2R+1)/2^{2R}\to0$ along some sequence of ranks $R\ge2$ tending to infinity, and ranks $R_k\to\infty$ with $s_{R_k}\le2^{R_k}$ supply such a sequence. Items 1 and 3 are stated as printed; the recurrence for $s_{R+1}$ is written with natural-number subtraction, which agrees with the integer identity because $s_{R+1}>2^{R+1}$ for all large $R$.

short.res-terminalhalf.label: res:terminalhalf
short.res-terminalhalf.title: finite approximations with vanishing scaled error
short.res-terminalhalf.relation_note: The Lean statement is the equivalence stated in the paragraph after the theorem: its right-to-left direction is the printed theorem, with $A\subseteq\mathbb N_{>0}$ written as $0\notin B$, and its left-to-right direction is the converse, with the approximants $M_j=j+1$ and $A_j=B\cap\{0,\ldots,j+1\}$.

short.res-cylinderhalf.label: res:cylinderhalf
short.res-cylinderhalf.title: unbounded shared-prefix families represent one half
short.res-cylinderhalf.relation_note: The Lean hypothesis has the printed content: a stage at depth $M$ with cutoff $K\le M$ consists of sets $A_1,\ldots,A_{B(M)}\subseteq\{2,\ldots,M\}$ with $1\le K_{A_k}(m)\le B(m)$ for $1\le m\le M$ and $K_{A_k}(M)=k$, agreeing on $\{1,\ldots,K\}$, whose suffix values are $E-k$ for one integer $E\ge B(M)$. The conclusion is the printed one, with $A\subseteq\Npos$ written as $0\notin A$.

long.thm-257-weighted.label: thm:257-weighted
long.thm-257-weighted.title: A weighted summability criterion
long.thm-257-weighted.relation_note: The first conjunct of the Lean claim and the displacement statement are the printed irrationality of $X_A(b)$ and the cofinal returns $0<\Delta_{b,A}(m)<\varepsilon$; the Lean claim adds a second conjunct, that if a set $H\subseteq\mathbb N_{>0}$ has finite weighted mass at $b=2$, then $X_A(b)$ is irrational for every $b\ge2$ and every infinite $A\subseteq H$.

long.prop-257-finite-witness-rule.label: prop:257-finite-witness-rule
long.prop-257-finite-witness-rule.title: realising finite monotone witness rules
long.prop-257-finite-witness-rule.relation_note: The Lean statement takes any upward-closed predicate $U$ on finite sets of naturals with $U(E)$ and not $U(\varnothing)$; the printed family $\mathcal U$ on subsets of $E$ is the case $U(S)\iff S\cap E\in\mathcal U$, which is upward closed because intersection with $E$ preserves inclusion, and then $U(\mathcal P\cap E)$ reads $\mathcal P\cap E\in\mathcal U$. The host $H$ omits $0$, so it is a set of positive integers; `Summable (Set.indicator H primeWeightedTerm)` is $W_{b,\mathcal P}(H)<\infty$ for nonnegative terms, and failure of summability of $1/a$ on $H$ is the printed divergence.

long.thm-supported-dichotomy.label: thm:supported-dichotomy
long.thm-supported-dichotomy.title: Support-restricted refinement
long.thm-supported-dichotomy.relation_note: The four Lean statements give the printed claims with the same zero-based coordinates: measure $2^{-|\N\smallsetminus J|}$ when $\N\smallsetminus J$ is finite, measure $0$ when it is infinite, injectivity of the coding map for every $J$, and perfectness for infinite $J$.

long.thm-greedy-survival.label: thm:greedy-survival
long.thm-greedy-survival.title: Membership equals greedy survival; the fatal-gap dichotomy

long.prop-canon.label: prop:canon
long.prop-canon.title: Uniqueness under the stated finite conditions
long.prop-canon.relation_note: Items (i), (ii) and (iii) are, in order, `IsStraddlePrefix.half_agrees_greedy`, `eq_halfGreedyPrefixSupport_of_critical_crossing` and `remainder_lt_gap_iff_eq_integerGreedyBits`, with the printed hypotheses. In (ii) the Lean conclusion is equality with the greedy prefix for $1/2$ computed in exact rational arithmetic through $c-1$; `paper_halfGreedyPrefixSupport_eq_greedy_inter_Icc` identifies that prefix with $G\cap\{2,\ldots,c-1\}$, which equals $G\cap\{1,\ldots,c-1\}$ because $w_1=1>1/2$ keeps $1$ out of $G$.

long.lem-collapse-mech.label: lem:collapse-mech
long.lem-collapse-mech.title: Carry and residual value
long.lem-collapse-mech.relation_note: The Lean identity $\operatorname{ihc}(A,N)=2^{N+1}\delta+\mathrm T(N+1)$ is as printed for $1\notin A$; the Lean bounds $0\le\mathrm T(m)\le2\sqrt m+4$ hold for every $A\subseteq\N$ and every $m$, without the hypothesis $1\notin A$, and the printed bounds are their case $m=N+1$.

long.lem-sqrt-witness.label: lem:sqrt-witness
long.lem-sqrt-witness.title: The terminal bound at square depths

long.prop-local-void.label: prop:local-void
long.prop-local-void.title: Limits of the specified local summaries
long.prop-local-void.relation_note: For (i) the identity $u(L)-v(L)=2^L(u_0-v_0)$ holds for every $L$ and every integer input sequence, and its residue form modulo $2^L$ is stated separately. For (ii), with $m\ge2$ and $0\le r\le h$, the Lean statements give the coefficients $c_r$, their common binary sum $h2^{-m}$, the common scaled tail $h2^{-(m-N)}$ at every $N<m$, the tail $r$ at $m$, the lower bound of $h+1$ labels for any exact label-and-decoder system, and the absence of a decoder from a state that is the same for every $r$. Item (iii) is the cited centred-completion statement, with $|e_{i+1}|\le2^{v_i+u-1}$ for every successor carry.

long.prop-exponent-gap.label: prop:exponent-gap
long.prop-exponent-gap.title: A bound for the reduced denominator

long.thm-greedy-survival-record.label: thm:greedy-survival-record
long.thm-greedy-survival-record.title: Membership equals greedy survival at every level

long.thm-real-form.label: thm:real-form
long.thm-real-form.title: Real (non-integer) form of the quotient identity

long.thm-dynamics.label: thm:dynamics
long.thm-dynamics.title: Exact recurrences for the three branches

long.thm-fatal-absorbing.label: thm:fatal-absorbing
long.thm-fatal-absorbing.title: Infinitely many greedy skips force membership

long.thm-seam-limit.label: thm:seam-limit
long.thm-seam-limit.title: The quotient remainders converge to the greedy deficit

long.thm-largest-skip-late.label: thm:largest-skip-late
long.thm-largest-skip-late.title: Keeping the largest skipped rank beyond two thirds

long.thm-middle-producer-escape.label: thm:middle-producer-escape
long.thm-middle-producer-escape.title: Two sufficient bounds at middle transitions

long.thm-middle-allright-defect.label: thm:middle-allright-defect
long.thm-middle-allright-defect.title: The tail inequality at a final middle transition
long.thm-middle-allright-defect.relation_note: The hypotheses are the printed ones: row $D$ is middle through its two branch inequalities, where the natural-number subtraction is exact since $p_D^-<2^{D+1}$, and each later row $s$ is right, written as $D_{s+1}=D_s\cup\{s\}$. Under them the Lean statements prove $C_D<\Theta_D$, with $C_D=4\,\mathrm{rem}(D)-p_D^--4$ identified separately, and the bounds $0\le\Theta_D\le|F_D|$; they add a second conclusion, $\tfrac12-X_{D_D}(2)<w_D$.

long.thm-two-sided-dyadic.label: thm:two-sided-dyadic
long.thm-two-sided-dyadic.title: A conditional two-sided dyadic bound
long.thm-two-sided-dyadic.relation_note: The Lean hypothesis is the printed pair of conditions at every row $s\ge5$, with the branches $\mathrm M$ and $\mathrm R$ written as their defining inequalities, and the conclusion $\mathrm{rem}(s)\le2^s$ or $o_s\le2^s$ at every row $s\ge5$ is the printed one.

long.thm-upper-reset-band.label: thm:upper-reset-band
long.thm-upper-reset-band.title: Upper-reset dyadic-band escape, checked for $`13\le d\le30`$
long.thm-upper-reset-band.relation_note: The first Lean statement is the printed implication from the band condition to $1/2\in\mathcal A$. The second gives the band disjunction, with reset charge $4o_d+p_d^+$, at every actual upper reset $13\le d\le30$ and every $0\le j\le d$, and the third states the successor remainders $\mathrm{rem}(14)=392$ through $\mathrm{rem}(31)=4187487147$. Together they have the printed hypotheses and conclusions.

long.thm-sqrt-bound-route.label: thm:sqrt-bound-route
long.thm-sqrt-bound-route.title: A square-root bound on the greedy carry

long.thm-pairwise-coprime.label: thm:pairwise-coprime
long.thm-pairwise-coprime.title: Pairwise-coprime support irrationality, Erdős 1968
long.thm-pairwise-coprime.relation_note: The Lean statement has the same hypotheses and conclusion as the printed one; its set $A$ may formally contain $0$, which no infinite pairwise-coprime set does, since $\gcd(0,a)=a$.

long.thm-lcm-gap-engine.label: thm:lcm-gap-engine
long.thm-lcm-gap-engine.title: Irrationality from a gap beyond the preceding least common multiple

long.thm-factorial-twopow-support.label: thm:factorial-twopow-support
long.thm-factorial-twopow-support.title: Factorial-support and $`2^k`$-support instances
long.thm-factorial-twopow-support.relation_note: The two Lean statements are the two irrationality claims for every $b\ge2$, indexed as printed by $k\ge0$. The remarks on the preceding least common multiples and gaps are elementary identities outside the Lean statements: $\operatorname{lcm}(1!,\ldots,k!)=k!$ with $(k+1)!-k!=k\,k!$, and $\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\ldots,2^{k-1})=2^{k-1}$ with $2^k-2^{k-1}=2^{k-1}$.

long.thm-multiples-support.label: thm:multiples-support
long.thm-multiples-support.title: Multiples-support irrationality via dilation
long.thm-multiples-support.relation_note: The Lean statements give the printed identity and irrationality for $b\ge2$ and $d\ge1$. The Lean set of multiples of $d$ also contains $0$, whose term $1/(b^0-1)$ is $0$ under the convention $1/0=0$.

long.thm-periodic-support.label: thm:periodic-support
long.thm-periodic-support.title: Periodic-support irrationality
long.thm-periodic-support.relation_note: The Lean statement takes a set $A\subseteq\N$ with a positive element and asks for $n+m\in A\iff n\in A$ at every $n\ge1$. The printed support is such a set, since it is nonempty and lies in $\Npos$, so the Lean theorem gives the printed conclusion. It is more general only in allowing $0\in A$, whose term is $0$ under the convention $1/0=0$.

long.thm-eventually-periodic.label: thm:eventually-periodic
long.thm-eventually-periodic.title: Eventually-periodic support irrationality
long.thm-eventually-periodic.relation_note: The Lean statement has the same hypotheses and conclusion as the printed one and also allows $0\in A$, whose term $1/(b^0-1)$ is $0$ under the convention $1/0=0$.

long.thm-residue-odd.label: thm:residue-odd
long.thm-residue-odd.title: Residue-class and odd-support irrationality
long.thm-residue-odd.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones, with the residue $c$ taken in $\N$, which covers every class modulo $m$. The Lean class also contains $0$ when $m\mid c$, and that term is $0$ under the convention $1/0=0$.

long.thm-signed-periodic.label: thm:signed-periodic
long.thm-signed-periodic.title: A formal dichotomy for signed periodic weights
long.thm-signed-periodic.relation_note: The dichotomy and the two sign versions, with $c_w(n)\ge0$ for every $n\ge1$ or $c_w(n)\le0$ for every $n\ge1$ and $c_w$ nonzero at arbitrarily large $n$, are the three Lean statements. The Lean weight is defined on $\N$ and periodic from $0$, which for the printed $w$ means setting $w(0)=w(m)$; the term at $a=0$ is $0$ under the convention $1/0=0$, and $c_w(n)$ uses only positive divisors.

long.thm-mersenne-channel-growth.label: thm:mersenne-channel-growth
long.thm-mersenne-channel-growth.title: Exponential growth of the reduced denominators

long.thm-mobius-lambert-identity.label: thm:mobius-lambert-identity
long.thm-mobius-lambert-identity.title: The Lambert-series identity for the Möbius function
long.thm-mobius-lambert-identity.relation_note: The Lean statement is the printed identity, summed over the positive integers. Absolute convergence follows from $|\mu(d)|/(2^d-1)\le2^{1-d}$.

long.cor-negative-mobius-overshoot.label: cor:negative-mobius-overshoot
long.cor-negative-mobius-overshoot.title: Negative-Möbius Boolean support overshoots $`1/2`$
long.cor-negative-mobius-overshoot.relation_note: The Lean statements give the identity $X_N(2)=\frac12+\sum_{d\ge2,\,\mu(d)=1}1/(2^d-1)$ and the conclusion $X_N(2)>\frac12$. The intermediate bound $X_N(2)\ge\frac12+\frac1{63}$ follows from the identity, since every term of the sum is nonnegative and the term at $d=6$ is $1/63$.

long.thm-half-skip-dichotomy.label: thm:half-skip-dichotomy
long.thm-half-skip-dichotomy.title: The half-skip dichotomy via Erdős–Borwein irrationality
long.thm-half-skip-dichotomy.relation_note: The equivalence is stated as printed, with $\N_{>0}\smallsetminus G$ written as the set of positive exponents omitted by the greedy rule for $1/2$. Irrationality of the full Mersenne sum $\sum_{n\ge1}1/(2^n-1)$, used in the forward direction, is the second Lean statement.

long.thm-nine-way-hub.label: thm:nine-way-hub
long.thm-nine-way-hub.title: Equivalent descriptions of half-membership
long.thm-nine-way-hub.relation_note: Items (1) to (5) and (7) are each proved equivalent to $1/2\in\mathcal A$, with branch $\mathrm R$ at row $s$ written as $D_{s+1}=D_s\cup\{s\}$ and the omitted ranks in (5) read off the greedy word of row $s_j$. Item (6) follows by combining the equivalence for (2) with the Lean equivalence between (2) and (6).

long.lem-eventually-right-impossible.label: lem:eventually-right-impossible
long.lem-eventually-right-impossible.title: The values on either side of an eventual right continuation
long.lem-eventually-right-impossible.relation_note: With the seam right from row $S\ge5$ on and support $u\cup\{D+1,\ldots,S-1\}$ at row $S$, where $u\subseteq\{2,\ldots,D-1\}$ and $2\le D<S$, the Lean statements prove $X_u(2)+R_D<\frac12$ for the cofinite continuation $u\cup\{D+1,D+2,\ldots\}$ and $\frac12<X_{u\cup\{D\}}(2)$ for the upper competitor.

long.lem-mersenne-tail-weight.label: lem:mersenne-tail-weight
long.lem-mersenne-tail-weight.title: Each Mersenne weight exceeds its remaining tail
long.lem-mersenne-tail-weight.relation_note: The Lean lower bound is $2^{-n}+\tfrac13\,4^{-n}<R_n$, sharper than the printed $2^{-n}<R_n$, and this bound, the identity $R_n=w_{n+1}+R_{n+1}$ and $R_n\le2w_{n+1}$ hold for every $n\ge0$; the printed statement takes $n\ge1$, where $2w_{n+1}<w_n$ and $R_n<w_n$ are as printed. The remark on the totient weights is the arithmetic $\varphi(4)/2^4+\varphi(5)/2^5=\frac14=\varphi(3)/2^3$, outside the Lean statements.

long.thm-greedy-survival-catalogue.label: thm:greedy-survival-catalogue
long.thm-greedy-survival-catalogue.title: Greedy survival and membership
long.thm-greedy-survival-catalogue.relation_note: The Lean statement is the displayed equivalence for the Mersenne weights and every real $x$, with the same hypotheses and conclusion as the printed one. The closing remark that the argument extends to other positive summable weights with $w_n>R_n$ describes the proof and has no Lean counterpart.

long.lem-rank-step-trichotomy.label: lem:rank-step-trichotomy
long.lem-rank-step-trichotomy.title: The two next-prefix intervals and their gap
long.lem-rank-step-trichotomy.relation_note: The Lean statements give the three alternatives for every real target $t$ (`isStraddlePrefix_step_trichotomy`); the left endpoint $X_{u\cup\{d+1\}}(2)$ of the upper interval equals $X_u(2)+w_{d+1}$ by `positiveMersenneSupportValue_insert`, since $d+1\notin u$. Disjointness is one line from $R_{d+1}<w_{d+1}$ (`mersenneTail_lt_weight`) and the strict inequalities defining the gap. For $t=1/2$, `IsStraddlePrefix.half_strict` makes every endpoint comparison strict and `IsStraddlePrefix.half_step_forced` gives the three cases as mutually exclusive.

long.lem-fatal-gap-exclusion.label: lem:fatal-gap-exclusion
long.lem-fatal-gap-exclusion.title: A greedy gap excludes every representation

long.lem-half-endpoint-kills.label: lem:half-endpoint-kills
long.lem-half-endpoint-kills.title: No finite Mersenne sum equals one half
long.lem-half-endpoint-kills.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same conclusions as the printed ones; the second holds for every finite $u$ and every $d\ge0$, where an index $0$ in $u$ contributes nothing to $X_u(2)$. Their proofs use the printed reasons: the reduced denominator of $X_u(2)$ is odd, and the full Mersenne sum is irrational.

long.lem-straddle-agrees-greedy.label: lem:straddle-agrees-greedy
long.lem-straddle-agrees-greedy.title: Straddle words are canonical: they agree with the greedy prefix
long.lem-straddle-agrees-greedy.relation_note: The Lean statement has the same hypotheses and conclusion as the printed one: it gives $n\in u\Leftrightarrow n\in G$ for $1\le n\le d$, which is $u=G\cap\{1,\ldots,d\}$.

long.thm-last-skip-iff-fatal.label: thm:last-skip-iff-fatal
long.thm-last-skip-iff-fatal.title: Last-skip iff local fatality: a pointwise criterion
long.thm-last-skip-iff-fatal.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones, with the omitted ranks taken as the positive ranks outside $G$.

long.lem-seam-upper-or-middle.label: lem:seam-upper-or-middle
long.lem-seam-upper-or-middle.title: Seam upper-or-middle classification
long.lem-seam-upper-or-middle.relation_note: The Lean statement has the same hypotheses and conclusion as the printed one: for $s\ge5$ the bit of index $s$ in the greedy word of row $s+1$ is zero exactly when branch $\mathrm U$ or branch $\mathrm M$ holds at $s$. The subtraction in the $\mathrm M$ inequality is natural-number subtraction, which agrees with the printed one because $p_s^-\le2(s-2)<2^{s+1}$.

long.lem-largest-false-rank-algebra.label: lem:largest-false-rank-algebra
long.lem-largest-false-rank-algebra.title: The exact gap at the largest omitted rank

long.thm-critical-dyadic-band.label: thm:critical-dyadic-band
long.thm-critical-dyadic-band.title: Reduction to the nearest dyadic boundary

long.thm-final-middle-cell.label: thm:final-middle-cell
long.thm-final-middle-cell.title: Excluding minus three at a final middle transition

long.lem-skipped-endpoint-trichotomy.label: lem:skipped-endpoint-trichotomy
long.lem-skipped-endpoint-trichotomy.title: The signed position of a skipped greedy prefix

long.lem-linear-channel-nogo.label: lem:linear-channel-nogo
long.lem-linear-channel-nogo.title: Linear functionals factoring through one value
long.lem-linear-channel-nogo.relation_note: The Lean factorisation $\Lambda(v)=\mathrm{ev}(v)\,w_0$ holds for a linear map $\Lambda$ into any $\mathbb Q$-vector space $W$ whose kernel contains $\ker(\mathrm{ev})$; the printed identity is its case $W=\mathbb Q$, $\Lambda=\ell_j$, where $w_0=\ell_j(e)$. The vanishing of every square minor of order at least two is the second Lean statement (a square matrix $(\ell_j(v_i))$ over an index set with at least two elements), and rank at most one follows from the $2\times2$ minors.

long.thm-two-thirds-band.label: thm:two-thirds-band
long.thm-two-thirds-band.title: Two-thirds band: exact localisation of post-take skip-unsafety

long.thm-sharp-fatal-gap.label: thm:sharp-fatal-gap
long.thm-sharp-fatal-gap.title: A weaker sufficient test against the remaining tail

long.lem-gap-mass-summability.label: lem:gap-mass-summability
long.lem-gap-mass-summability.title: Summability of one gap length per level
long.lem-gap-mass-summability.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones: $g_n>0$ for $n\ge1$, and the tail bound for every $N\ge0$. They also record that $\sum_n g_n$ converges and that its tails tend to $0$.

long.lem-half-divisor-unit-drop.label: lem:half-divisor-unit-drop
long.lem-half-divisor-unit-drop.title: The effect of adding one divisor
long.lem-half-divisor-unit-drop.relation_note: The Lean identity $c_{A\cup\{d\}}(m)=c_A(m)+\mathbf 1_{d\mid m}$ holds for every positive $m$, every set $A\subseteq\mathbb N$, finite or infinite, and every $d\notin A$; the printed statement is its case of a finite support $D_0$ and $d=N+1$. The value $1$ at $m=2(N+1)$ is also stated separately for finite binary words.

long.thm-tempered-orbit-rigidity.label: thm:tempered-orbit-rigidity
long.thm-tempered-orbit-rigidity.title: Uniqueness of an integer recurrence with a vanishing scaled limit
long.thm-tempered-orbit-rigidity.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones, with rationality written as $X_c=p/v$ for an integer $p$ and a positive integer $v$. Uniqueness for each fixed $v$ follows at once from $u(N)=v\,T_c(N)$.

long.lem-tail-transfer.label: lem:tail-transfer
long.lem-tail-transfer.title: Changing finitely many support elements
long.lem-tail-transfer.relation_note: The Lean statements say that, for every $M\ge0$, $X_A(b)$ is irrational exactly when $X_{A\cap(M,\infty)}(b)$ is. The printed lemma follows in one line: sets with finite symmetric difference agree above some $M$, so irrationality passes from $X_A(b)$ to the common tail and back to $X_B(b)$.

long.lem-dyadic-excess-reformulation.label: lem:dyadic-excess-reformulation
long.lem-dyadic-excess-reformulation.title: An integer test for the interval between the dyadic and Mersenne weights
long.lem-dyadic-excess-reformulation.relation_note: The Lean statements prove both equivalences for every integer $p$, every $L\ge1$ and every $n\ge0$, so the hypothesis $p>0$ is unnecessary; the second right-hand side is written as $0<E$ and $2E<p$. A third statement is the second equivalence for the half-greedy residual $r_n(1/2)$.

long.lem-denominator-sandwich.label: lem:denominator-sandwich
long.lem-denominator-sandwich.title: The odd denominator survives dyadic subtraction
long.lem-denominator-sandwich.relation_note: The Lean statements take integers $p,r$ with no sign condition on $p/2^c-r/D$. `dyadicResidualIntNumerator_coprime_oddDenominator` shows that $pD-2^cr$ is coprime to $D$ when $D$ is odd and $\gcd(r,D)=1$, and `dyadicResidualInt_denominator_sandwich` then gives both divisibilities for the reduced denominator of $(pD-2^cr)/(2^cD)$, so the printed lemma is their one-line composition. `dyadicResidual_denominator_sandwich` is the special case $p,r\ge0$ with $2^cr\le pD$.

long.lem-denominator-survival.label: lem:denominator-survival
long.lem-denominator-survival.title: A guaranteed divisor of a reduced denominator
long.lem-denominator-survival.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones; $C/\gcd(C,h)$ is an exact quotient, so natural-number division agrees with the printed one.

long.lem-mixed-prime-power-layer.label: lem:mixed-prime-power-layer
long.lem-mixed-prime-power-layer.title: Commuting prime-power differences
long.lem-mixed-prime-power-layer.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones, with the commutation proved for every $p,e$ and every $g$ defined on all of $\mathbb N$. The right side of the mixed identity is written as $c_{A'}(n)$ with $A'=\{d:\gcd(d,pq)=1,\ p^eq^fd\in A\}$, which equals $\sum_{d\mid n}\mathbf 1_A(p^eq^fd)$ because every divisor of $n$ is prime to $pq$.

long.thm-master-dichotomy.title: Nonmembership of one half and a finite fatal gap
long.thm-master-dichotomy.relation_note: The Lean statement has the same hypotheses and conclusion as the printed one, in the form $1/2\in\mathcal A$ exactly when no such $d$ and $u$ exist. A second Lean statement records the direction from nonmembership to a gap as the disjunction that $1/2\in\mathcal A$ or such a gap exists.

long.thm-perturbed-family-maximality.label: thm:perturbed-family-maximality
long.thm-perturbed-family-maximality.title: Perturbed-family maximality and the three-branch recurrence
long.thm-perturbed-family-maximality.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones. Under $B<g$, `prefixChoice_maximal` bounds every admissible updated value by $t$ of the chosen element, which is admissible by `above_newSum_le_capacity_iff` when $4o+p_+\le g$ and by `below_newSum_le_capacity` otherwise, and `prefixRemainder_eq_capacity_sub_choice` identifies the remainder before the weight $W$ with $C'$ minus that value. `nextRemainder_trichotomy` gives the three remainders, whose natural-number subtractions agree with the printed ones because $p_-\le B<g$ and because of each case's inequality.

long.record-257bm-i-mob.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones, with the identity written as the Dirichlet convolution $\mu*c_A=\mathbf 1_A$ on the positive integers. long.record-257bm-i-bridge.label: record:257bm-i-bridge
long.record-257bm-i-bridge.title: The support series as a coefficient series
long.record-257bm-i-bridge.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones, for every set $A\subseteq\mathbb N$; an element $0$ contributes to neither side. They also give $c_A(n)\le\tau(n)$, $c_A(n)\le n$, and the resulting criterion that $X_A(2)$ is rational exactly when, for some positive integer $v$, the recurrence $u(N+1)=2u(N)-v\,c_A(N+1)$ has an integer solution with $u(N)/2^N\to0$.

long.record-257rig-i2.relation_note: The first Lean statement replaces infinitude by the presence of two distinct positive elements of $A$: if $X_A(2)=p/2^c$ and $\sum_{a\in A}1/a$ converges, then $\sum_{a\in A}1/a>1$; the printed statement for infinite $A$ is the second Lean statement.

long.record-257rig-i3.label: record:257rig-i3
long.record-257rig-i3.title: Unboundedness of a positive shifted recurrence
long.record-257rig-i3.relation_note: The unboundedness of $u$ is the second Lean statement as printed; the Lean statements add the quantitative bound $1+v\,|F|\le2u(L-c-1)$ for every finite $F\subseteq A$ whose elements divide some $L>c$, which drives the proof, and, whenever $X_A(2)=p/(2^cv)$, the existence of such a positive unbounded sequence, $u(n)=v\sum_{r\ge1}c_A(c+n+r)2^{-r}$.

long.lem-tr-forced-greedy.relation_note: The Lean statements have the same hypotheses and conclusions as the printed ones, and the uniqueness is stronger: every set $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ with $\sum_{n\in A}w_n^{(J)}=1/2$ is the greedy support, with no restriction to $A\subseteq\{2,3,\ldots\}$.
